1_the_token_disagrees.next: The established method in this tree is a depth bisection against the oracle's per-layer activations (results/abi3/deepseek_v41_oracle_depth_bisection_deep.json is the V4.1 precedent).  At 7,241 s per walk the loop is expensive, so the bisection wants instrumenting once rather than re-walking per hypothesis.
1_the_token_disagrees.why_this_is_NOT_the_reduced_vehicle's_pr: The reduced V4.1 cells disagree because their router is near-tied: the reduced fixture's first-token margin is 0.00515, so sub-ulp differences at ffn_norm flip a routing decision and the token with it.  The SHIPPED release's first-token margin is **2.494688**, 484 times larger.  A disagreement at that margin cannot be amplified rounding, so this is a real defect in the lowering or the execution -- which makes it diagnosable rather than attributable, and is exactly why the shipped vehicle was worth reaching.

2_decode_step_1_refuses.reading: GROUPED_CONCAT's output view declares 128 rows and its inputs sum to 4,224 = 4,096 + 128 on axis 0.  4,096 is a compressed-prefix plane and 128 is the sliding window, so the join is the prefix-plus-window concatenation and the output was sized as the WINDOW alone.  Prefill did not hit it; decode does, which points at the phase-dependent form of the join rather than at the join itself.

what_happened: The SHIPPED DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ROM wafer, built at an 8,192-token deployment context, completed a 32-token prefill and emitted a token.  That is the first time the shipped V4.1 path has produced a token on the accelerator at all; every prior attempt refused during prefill.
what_this_run_establishes: the Engram row-scale width fix is load-bearing: prefill now passes the EMBED_LOOKUP that refused with '(32, 24, 1); expected (768, 8)'
the 8,192-token context avoids the candidate-mask 32-bit stride overflow, as predicted from the descriptor tables rather than hoped for
the shipped V4.1 graph executes 32 rows of prefill end to end on the ROM wafer
